introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Citizenship Education 2 (0562), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2024. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- You are required to answer FOUR questions choosing QUESTION 1 and THREE others from Sections A, B, and C.
- All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to different parts of questions are indicated.
- Extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Question 1 (compulsory)**

Study the following unpublished article on environmental degradation and then answer questions (a) to (d) which follow (the maximum mark for each sub question is indicated in brackets).

> There has been growing concern about the rapid deterioration of the natural environment resulting from a combination of natural and human factors. The ever increasing population of the earth has created a situation where human activities such as agriculture and industrialization are constantly damaging the natural environment and creating serious risks for the wellbeing and survival of humanity itself...
>
> The high pace of environmental degradation is most noticeable in towns and cities where overcrowding poses serious problems of waste management. In the cities of Yaounde and Douala, for example, council authorities have often resorted to the destruction of slums in order to improve on drainage and reduce environmental pollution. Even in rural communities, certain traditional agricultural practices continue to have a damaging effect on the environment, due to ignorance and illiteracy. In Kopo village, for instance, there is indiscriminate felling of trees to create space for new farms in a bid to replace those considered infertile, as well as a massive use of farm chemicals by farmers.
>
> There is therefore an urgent need for behavioural change to be able to maintain a healthy environment for both present and future generations. This brings to light the importance of education and sensitisation. It is for these reasons that educational authorities have taken several measures to enable students cultivate the habit of environmental protection by first of all taking good care of the school environment...
>
> As a matter of fact, environmental protection is not only the responsibility of state governments but also that of homes and local communities. It is regrettable that in many homes, even basic rules of hygiene and sanitation have been pushed to the background. This gap in home education has a serious negative effect on environmental protection. In fact, it is embarrassing to note that issues of basic hygiene and sanitation have often led to quarrels, even among siblings, and have generated several conflicts among neighbours.

*Source: Unpublished*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Identify the **two** major components of the natural environment whose deterioration is being referred to in **line 1**.

(ii) State **one** natural factor that has been responsible for the "rapid deterioration of the natural environment" (**line 1**).

(iii) Give **two** ways in which industrialization contributes in damaging the environment.

[(2 + 1 + 2) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The two major components (2 marks)**

The natural environment is made up of:

1. The **physical (non-living) component**: air, water, soil and land, climate.
2. The **biological (living) component**: plants (vegetation, forests) and animals (wildlife).

*(Other acceptable pairs: land and water; air and water; plants and animals. Any two correct components earn the marks.)*

**(ii) One natural factor (1 mark)**

Any one of: **floods** and heavy rainfall, **volcanic eruptions**, **drought**, **landslides** and soil erosion caused by rain, earthquakes or storms.

**(iii) Two ways industrialization damages the environment (2 marks)**

1. **Air pollution**: factories release smoke and harmful gases that pollute the air, cause acid rain and contribute to global warming.
2. **Water and soil pollution**: factories discharge toxic wastes and chemicals into rivers, lakes and the soil, which kills aquatic life and makes water unsafe.

*(Other acceptable ways: clearing land and forests to build factories; noise pollution; huge quantities of solid waste; heavy use of raw materials and energy.)*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) State any **one** contribution made by city councils to protect the environment apart from the one mentioned in the text.

(ii) Give **two** reasons why towns continue to attract more population in spite of their environmental problems.

(iii) State any **two** basic rules of personal hygiene which constitute the subject of home education.

[(1 + 2 + 2) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) One contribution of city councils (1 mark)**

The text mentions the destruction of slums to improve drainage. Another contribution is, for example:

- **collecting and disposing of household waste** (refuse collection, dumping sites), or
- **cleaning and maintaining drains and gutters**, or
- **planting trees and creating green spaces**, or
- **making and enforcing sanitation by-laws** (for example against dumping refuse in the street), or
- **sensitising the population** on cleanliness and environmental protection.

*(Any one.)*

**(ii) Two reasons why towns continue to attract people (2 marks)**

1. **Job and business opportunities**: factories, offices, markets and services offer employment and income that are scarce in villages.
2. **Better social amenities**: towns have more schools, hospitals, electricity, pipe-borne water, roads and entertainment.

*(Other acceptable reasons: access to administrative services; better housing and transport; hope of a better standard of living.)*

**(iii) Two basic rules of personal hygiene (2 marks)**

1. **Wash hands with soap and clean water** before eating and after using the toilet.
2. **Bathe regularly and keep the body, hair, nails and clothes clean.**

*(Other acceptable rules: brush the teeth every day; use latrines or toilets properly; keep food and drinking water covered and clean; sleep under clean bedding.)*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Identify any **two** environmental problems that would likely be created by farmers in Kopo village, mentioned in **line 9** of the above text.

(ii) Suggest a reason for the use of farm chemicals by farmers in Kopo village mentioned in the passage.

(iii) Imagining that you are from Kopo village, what environmental friendly actions would you advise your village to take in resolving the problems identified in c (i) above?

[(2 + 1 + 2) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two environmental problems (2 marks)**

The passage says that farmers in Kopo village fell trees indiscriminately to create new farms and use large amounts of farm chemicals. The likely problems are:

1. **Deforestation**, which leads to soil erosion, loss of wildlife habitats (loss of biodiversity), reduced rainfall and flooding.
2. **Pollution of soil and water** by farm chemicals (fertilisers, pesticides), which kills useful organisms, damages the soil and contaminates streams and drinking water.

*(Other acceptable problems: loss of soil fertility; destruction of plants and animals; harm to the health of farmers and villagers.)*

**(ii) A reason for using farm chemicals (1 mark)**

The farmers use fertilisers to **restore or increase the fertility of poor soils** and so obtain better harvests, and pesticides to **kill pests and weeds** that reduce yields. (The passage also links such practices to **ignorance and illiteracy**.)

**(iii) Environment-friendly actions to advise (2 marks)**

1. **Replant trees** (reforestation) and practise **agroforestry**, and **stop cutting trees without control** and clearing new land when old farms can be improved.
2. **Use organic manure and compost, crop rotation and fallowing** to keep the soil fertile, and **use farm chemicals only in the recommended quantities**, as advised by agricultural extension workers.

*(Other acceptable actions: terracing or contour farming against erosion; avoiding bush burning; training farmers through sensitisation campaigns.)*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) State **two** ways in which the environment is important to man.

(ii) Describe the efforts made towards environmental protection by the government services in charge of the environment in Cameroon.

[(2 + 3) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two ways the environment is important to man (2 marks)**

1. It **provides the basic needs of life**: air to breathe, water to drink, food from farms, forests and rivers, and land for shelter.
2. It **provides raw materials and energy** (timber, minerals, water for electricity, firewood) used in industry and the economy, and **medicinal plants** for health.

*(Other acceptable ways: it regulates the climate and rainfall; it offers beauty, recreation and tourism; it is a source of income.)*

**(ii) Efforts of the government services in charge of the environment (3 marks)**

The Government of Cameroon acts through the **ministry in charge of the environment** and other services such as those in charge of forests and wildlife. Their efforts include:

1. **Making and enforcing laws and regulations** on environmental management, for example the requirement of **environmental impact studies** before big projects and the control of **pollution and waste**, including limits on non-biodegradable plastic packaging.
2. **Protecting nature**: creating and managing **protected areas** (national parks, forest and wildlife reserves) and promoting **reforestation** and tree-planting campaigns, and the fight against desertification in the northern part of the country.
3. **Education and sensitisation**: organising environmental awareness campaigns, the celebration of **World Environment Day (5 June)**, and encouraging environmental clubs in schools.
4. **International cooperation**: signing and applying international agreements on the environment, climate change and biodiversity.

*Conclusion:* these efforts show that the State is committed to a healthy environment, although their success also depends on the cooperation of citizens.
